highlightAliases.old: HLA-B1502 and HLA-A3101 (most common in South Asian ancestry) — carriers are at increased risk of severe skin reactions such as Stevens–Johnson syndrome (p1065).
highlightAliases.new: HLA-B15:02 is linked to carbamazepine- and oxcarbazepine-associated SJS/TEN. HLA-A31:01 is associated with several carbamazepine hypersensitivity reactions and occurs across multiple ancestries. The genes do not have the same geographic distribution (p1065, CPIC).

highlightAliases.old: Osteoarthritis (OA): 60% of adults ≥65 yr have arthritis/chronic joint pain (p1066); intra-articular steroid (40–80 mg depot preparation, verified against the page image) is more effective than placebo in the short term (<3 months), long-term benefit not well established; hyaluronic acid typically 1–5 injections; platelet-rich plasma (PRP) shows efficacy up to 12 months in some studies (p1067)
highlightAliases.new: Osteoarthritis (OA): 60% of adults ≥65 yr have arthritis/chronic joint pain (p1066); for knee OA, intra-articular steroid (40–80 mg depot preparation) is more effective than placebo in the short term (<3 months), long-term benefit not well established; hyaluronic acid typically 1–5 injections; platelet-rich plasma (PRP) shows promising efficacy in knee OA up to 12 months in some studies; hip HA/PRP efficacy needs further study (p1067)

highlightAliases.old: CDC caution thresholds: reassess benefit/risk >50 MME/day; avoid >90 MME/day (p1060)
highlightAliases.new: Before increasing to 50 MME/day or more, pause to reassess benefits and risks and consider precautions. The 2022 CDC guideline for outpatient pain treatment uses dosage as a guidepost and rejects an inflexible 90-MME ceiling. It excludes cancer-related pain treatment, palliative care and end-of-life care (p1060 discusses the 2016 guideline).

highlightAliases.old: Gabapentinoids/sodium channel blockers (carbamazepine, oxcarbazepine) for neuropathic pain; genotype screening may be indicated for HLA-B*1502 and HLA-A*3101 (most common in South Asian ancestry) — carriers are at risk of severe skin reactions such as Stevens–Johnson syndrome; carbamazepine is a potent CYP450 inducer (interacts with warfarin, lithium) (p1065)
highlightAliases.new: Carbamazepine and oxcarbazepine are sodium-channel blockers used for selected neuropathic pain syndromes. HLA-B*15:02 increases the risk of SJS/TEN with either drug and is more frequent in several East, Southeast and South Asian populations. HLA-A*31:01 is associated with a broader range of carbamazepine reactions in several ancestries. Carbamazepine induces CYP enzymes and can reduce warfarin exposure. Combined lithium and carbamazepine can cause neurotoxicity (p1065, CPIC).

highlightAliases.old: Start at about 25% to 50% of the dose given to younger patients; the CDC recommends carefully weighing risk/benefit above 50 MME/day and avoiding doses above 90 MME/day (p1060).
highlightAliases.new: The chapter suggests lower initial opioid doses in older adults, often 25–50% of a younger adult's dose (p1060). Choose the drug and dose for renal function, frailty and prior exposure. CDC 2022 recommends reassessment before reaching 50 MME/day and individualized decisions rather than a fixed 90-MME ceiling.

highlightAliases.old: HLA-B*1502 and HLA-A*3101 (most common in South Asian ancestry) — carriers are at increased risk of severe skin reactions such as Stevens–Johnson syndrome (p1065).
highlightAliases.new: HLA-B15:02 is linked to carbamazepine- and oxcarbazepine-associated SJS/TEN. HLA-A31:01 is associated with several carbamazepine hypersensitivity reactions and occurs across multiple ancestries. The genes do not have the same geographic distribution (p1065, CPIC).

highlightAliases.old: Benzodiazepines (eg clonazepam) for neuropathic pain: daily use >30 days risks physiologic dependence — taper, don't stop abruptly; tracked as lorazepam milligram equivalents (LMEs) in PDMPs (p1065)
highlightAliases.new: Regular benzodiazepine use can cause physical dependence within days to weeks. The book highlights daily use beyond 30 days. When stopping a drug such as clonazepam in a physically dependent patient, taper gradually. Some prescription monitoring programs track lorazepam milligram equivalents (p1065, FDA boxed warning).

highlightAliases.old: Daily use for more than 30 days can cause physical dependence, so reduce gradually if stopping.
